messages.subject: Re: outfit.z seems wrong
parts:
I'm not entirely sure what to make of this since the eRm package appears to follow the same format that mirt does in calculating these statistics. Copied from there code we can see that the two implementation are exactly the same (independently written, might I add, since I didn't use their code as a reference):

############################
i.outfitMSQ <- ifit/idf

  qsq.outfitMSQ <- (colSums(Cmat/Vmat^2, na.rm=TRUE)/idf^2) - 1/idf
  q.outfitMSQ <- sqrt(qsq.outfitMSQ)

  isumVmat<-colSums(Vmat)
  i.infitMSQ <- colSums(sq.res*Vmat, na.rm = TRUE)/isumVmat

  qsq.infitMSQ <- colSums(Cmat-Vmat^2, na.rm=TRUE)/isumVmat^2
  q.infitMSQ <- sqrt(qsq.infitMSQ)

  i.outfitZ <- (i.outfitMSQ^(1/3) - 1)*(3/q.outfitMSQ)+(q.outfitMSQ/3) # corr. rh 2011-06-15
  i.infitZ  <- (i.infitMSQ^(1/3)  - 1)*(3/q.infitMSQ) +(q.infitMSQ/3)  # hint from rainer alexandrowicz

############################

In fact, comparing the two models gives very close results, the differences being a) the estimator (MML versus CML) and b) how extreme response patterns are handled. Here's a quick comparison use mirt version 0.7.4 and eRm version 0.15-1: 

############################

> library(eRm)
> res <- RM(raschdat1)
> p.res <- person.parameter(res)
> erm <- itemfit(p.res)
> 
> library(mirt)

> mod <- mirt(raschdat1, 1, 'Rasch')

> mirt <- itemfit(mod, method = 'ML')
> vals <- data.frame(mirt$outfit, erm$i.outfitMSQ, mirt$z.outfit, erm$i.outfitZ, 
+               mirt$infit, erm$i.infitMSQ, mirt$z.infit, erm$i.infitZ)
> head(vals)

So the ultimate question comes to this: who do we think is more right, Winsteps or eRm? Maybe contacting the Winsteps crew or Patrick Mair would help clear up the issue. 

Phil
